ArtifactRef.description: Content-addressed bytes. The artifact is durable before any event references it; readers verify sha256 and length.

AudioPart.description: Recorded (non-realtime) audio, e.g. a channel voice note. Only adapters that declare audio input accept it; others fail pre-dispatch with content_unsupported. Realtime sessions are out of scope.

transcript.description: Host-produced transcript, shown only to adapters without audio input when the agent opts in.

Budget.description: Limits checked before every model_request. Unknown usage counts at its conservative upper bound.

CallId.description: Tool call id; may be provider-issued. The effect key is derived: <branch_id of the tool_call event>:<call_id>.

CallerAddress.description: A thread outside the host team (Phase 2). It may only send and ask a host member, and a host member answers it only by reply or bounce.

agent.description: The caller thread's agent: a host rule's from, and the deciding rule's key.

CitationPart.description: Annotates the text part immediately before it. source_id is a URL (web), doc_id (knowledge, with version), document artifact sha256 (document) or call_id (tool_result). ref and span name the exact cited bytes.

output.description: The latest task's answer; structured output is its accepted value as RFC 8785 JSON text.

observed_is_upper_bound.description: true when unknown usage was counted at its conservative upper bound.

owner_thread_id.description: Required exactly when scope is ancestor: the ancestor thread whose budget refused the reservation.

scope.description: Which budget refused the reservation. run and thread: this thread's own budget (the owner is the envelope thread_id, so owner_thread_id is absent). ancestor: a budget of an ancestor thread in the agent tree, named by owner_thread_id. hop (Phase 2): the host rule's per-hop cap on a host member's turn, budget id hop:<branch_id>:<turn opener event_id>; only that turn ends.

to_thread.description: The lead only: members can't hand off.

HostedToolPart.description: A provider-executed tool use and its result, inside one model attempt. The execution owner is the provider: it is never turned into a tool_call or dispatched locally. ref holds the exact provider blocks; readable citations follow as citation parts.

ImagePart.description: An image the model sees. Bytes are always an artifact; width and height are what the adapter needs for scaling (computer use coordinates).

InputPart.description: What a user or channel may send. No tool_use: user content never enters dispatch.

Int.description: JSON integer in the cross-language safe range.

JsonValue.description: Any validated JSON value (tool input, model params, MCP payloads). Numbers follow.

MailAddress.description: A member at one generation, the team log (the operator's replies and notifications), or a caller thread outside the host team.

MailEnvelope.description: One mail, as the sender's message_sent records it and every receipt copies it byte for byte. member_parked is a one-time, non-consuming park notice.

ask_id.description: ask: its own mail_id. reply: the ask it answers. bounce: the open ask it closes as member_ended, or as failed for turn_failed.

causal.description: The request or event that caused this mail: the call's tool_call, the operator_request, the member's idle or end event, or the refused mail's mail_refused.

code.description: bounce: why. stale_member and member_ended answer a mail_refused; turn_failed (Phase 2) answers an ask a host member's failed turn took.

error.description: turn_failed only: why the host member's turn failed; the ask closes failed with it.

monitor_id.description: The monitor this notification fires; its row is deleted in the same append.

result.description: member_settled (completed), member_ended (terminal), or an ask's bounce (the ended member's result).

MailId.description: <sender branch_id>:<call_id or request_id> for mail a call sends; <sender branch_id>:<event_id of the message_sent> for mail the runtime sends (notifications, bounces, lead-close cancels).

MailSender.description: The sending member, the operator request, or a caller thread. Written by the fenced writer; never an actor.

MemberErrorCode.description: A failed member's code: the host API RunErrorCode, plus pin_unavailable and pin_mismatch for a failed rebind, and setup_failed for a member whose setup kept failing.

MemberName.description: <agent>-<k>, k counting that agent's members in the team from 1. The lead's name is its agent name.

MemberRef.description: One member of one team. Immutable.

generation.description: Changes only through a supervised restart; 1 until then.

MonitorId.description: <watcher branch_id>:<event_id of the registering event>:<target name>; the target name is task for a start's task monitor. Derived, never generated.

Principal.description: A verified identity, normalized by the host. issuer names the identity authority (e.g. slack:T024BE7LD, api), tenant the isolation scope.

Provenance.description: Causal, not structural: who originated the work and which request it belongs to. One turn's opening batch shares one (principal, root_request).

principal.description: The verified originating principal: the root run's input principal, or the operator's.

root_request.description: The lead run's user_input, or the team log's operator_request. Budgets roll up to its run budget.

via.description: The member hops. Provenance only: authority, credentials and grants never transfer.

ReasoningPart.description: Opaque provider continuation material (Anthropic thinking or redacted_thinking with its signature, OpenAI reasoning items with encrypted content). ref holds the exact provider bytes/JSON. Never rendered as text and never required in a UI. Render v1 emits the part as recorded; an adapter that cannot send it back fails with continuation_unsupported, never drops it silently. Only settings_changed{reasoning_carryover: omit_prior} omits earlier parts.

summary.description: Provider-supplied readable summary, for display only.

RequestId.description: One operator request: a team.start, send, ask, wait or cancel call.

RequestRef.description: An event in another thread's log, by thread and event id.

ResultPart.description: Ordered, mixed text and media of a tool result. No tool_use.

Span.description: Half-open range [start, end) in UTF-8 BYTE offsets of the referenced text or artifact bytes. Both ends fall on character boundaries. Python and TypeScript convert from their native string indices; a span never means code units.

StoredMemberResult.description: What a settled member returned, as member_idle, member_ended, notifications and member_observed record it. Public result APIs hydrate a ref'd output (sha256 and length verified); the audit feed returns it as stored.

TextBody.description: Inline text up to the inline cap, else a content-addressed artifact written before the append.

TextOrContent.description: Exactly one of plain text or ordered input parts.

TextOrRef.description: Exactly one of inline text or an artifact ref.

TimeMs.description: Unix epoch milliseconds. Informational; never used for ordering.

ToolUsePart.description: A locally dispatchable call proposed by the model. Only model_response and model_response_recovered may carry it; a tool_call must match one.

TurnFailure.description: Why a host member's turn failed (Phase 2). Only that turn ends: its unanswered asks close failed and the member goes back to idle.

code.description: Mapped from the failed turn's turn_completed: its reason (max_turns, max_output, stop_hook_limit, context_exhausted, output_invalid, input_denied, model_unavailable, budget_exhausted for the hop cap or the caller's run budget, interrupted for a turn recovery closed), or for reason error its code (content_unsupported, continuation_unsupported, transport_fence_unsupported, secret_in_provider_output), else model_error.

Uuid.description: Lowercase UUID string. Writers MUST generate UUIDv7; readers accept any lowercase UUID, so the version is not an admission rule.

code.description: Only with reason error: the request needed a part the model doesn't declare (content_unsupported) or another provider's continuation (continuation_unsupported), found before any model_request; or the adapter refused the send because its transport bypasses the fence (transport_fence_unsupported, never retried); or the response held a registered secret in provider material that is replayed byte-exact and so can't be redacted (secret_in_provider_output: nothing of it is stored, never retried); or a team member's rebind failed before its first model request: its definition, a tool or a model is not registered here (pin_unavailable), the rebuilt config_hash differs (pin_mismatch), or setting it up kept failing (setup_failed).

stop_reason.description: Only end_turn, stop_sequence and refusal complete a turn; tool_use dispatches; max_tokens continues; pause_turn re-requests with the paused content as-is, up to context.max_pause_continuations; context_window_exceeded ends the turn context_exhausted; other (a reason the adapter can't name) ends it error. Never success for the last two.

envelope.description: Byte for byte the sender's message_sent envelope, provenance included, so every rule about received mail reads only this log.

a2a.description: Only with source api: the A2A message this input arrived as, recorded so a resend of the same messageId finds its run. claims is what the calling partner asserted about provenance and is untrusted: it never grants authority, never picks a budget and never becomes provenance.principal, which is always the authenticated principal of the call.

budget.description: The budget of the run this input starts.

client_message_id.description: The id a web UI gave this message (the AI SDK UIMessage id or the AG-UI message id), recorded by the UI routes so a retry finds its run and a snapshot names the message as the client does. Not rendered.

delivery_event_id.description: The channel_delivery or schedule_fired event this input came from.

mail_id.description: Exactly with source team_task: the task mail this input consumes (its row becomes consumed in this append).

causes.description: The tool_result_late events in this same append that woke the thread.

envelope.description: Byte for byte the sender's message_sent envelope, provenance included, so every rule about received mail reads only this log.
